title: Visits to Zaki Nassif Museum in Mashgharah
summary: On the 24th of September 2016, heading a delegation from the Walid Ibn Talal Association, H. E. Mrs. Leila El Solh Hamade visited the Zaki Nassif Museum and Cultural center in Mashghara. A guided tour of the site allowed Her Excellency to…
content:
On the 24th of September 2016, heading a delegation from the Walid Ibn Talal Association, H. E. Mrs. Leila El Solh Hamade visited the Zaki Nassif Museum and Cultural center in Mashghara. A guided tour of the site allowed Her Excellency to learn about the history of the building and as well to discover the Center and the APSAD’s Music school.

Later on that day, the site was visited by the Governor of Beirut, Mr. Ziad Chebib, the President of the Arab Open University – Lebanon, Dr. Fairouz Farah Sarkis and Mr. Massoud Al Ashkar.

All the visitors expressed their admiration of the great efforts made by APSAD and its president Mrs. Raya Daouk to restore the house of the great Lebanese composer Zaki Nassif, transforming it to a historical, cultural and educational site.

title: Grand opening of Zaki Nassif Museum and cultural center and the Music School of APSAD
summary: Grand opening of Zaki Nassif Museum and cultural center and the Music School of APSAD in Mashghra- west bekaa The Association for The Protection of Natural Sites and Old Buildings in Lebanon (APSAD) is pleased to announce the full…
content:
Grand opening of

Zaki Nassif Museum and cultural center and the Music School of APSAD

in Mashghra- west bekaa

The Association for The Protection of Natural Sites and Old Buildings in Lebanon (APSAD) is pleased to announce the full renovation of Zaki Nassif’s old traditional house in his hometown, Mashghara. Zaki Nassif’s heirs had donated the property to APSAD in December 2012, for the purpose of rehabilitating it as a museum and a cultural center. It will serve also as APSAD Music School.

On the occasion of zaki nassif’s Centennial, the grand opening of the center will take place on May 21, 2016 at 4:00 pm, under the patronage of His Excellency the Minister of Culture, Mr. Raymond Araiji.

APSAD strongly believes that the achievement of this project in Western Bekaa represents a model of cooperation among philanthropists, actors of the civil society and major Lebanese artists, who left, beside their cultural legacy, a traditional Lebanese house that will survive their memory. This model represents, in this particular case, a cornerstone for the dissemination of culture in general, and music in particular, in remote Lebanese regions.

title: LIU and APSAD meet to discuss possible cooperation
summary: A meeting has been held on the 17th of April 2015 between the President of the Lebanese International University (LIU) Dr. Abdel Raheem Mourad and the President of The Association for Protecting Natural Sites and Old Buildings ( APSAD)…
content:
A meeting has been held on the 17th of April 2015 between the President of the Lebanese International University (LIU) Dr. Abdel Raheem Mourad and the President of The Association for Protecting Natural Sites and Old Buildings ( APSAD) Mrs.Raya Daouk and APSAD’s executive committee member Dr. Nabil Nassif. Discussions took place about future cooperation between LIU and APSAD to promote the future "Zaki Nassif School of Music (ZNSM)" in Mashgharah – West Bekaa, expected to be inaugurated in September 2015.

It was agreed to have follow-up meetings in view of establishing a common network of schools and universities operating in the Bekaa region that will profit from the programs and cultural impact of the ZNSM.

title: Janneh dam
summary: Meetings to stop the construction of the planned Janneh dam in Nahr Brahim until further serious studyThree meetings were held about Janneh dam (Adonis, Nahr Ibrahim).The first two at the residence of the APSAD’s President Ms. Raya Daouk…
content:
Meetings to stop the construction of the planned Janneh dam in Nahr Brahim until further serious study

Three meetings were held about Janneh dam (Adonis, Nahr Ibrahim).

The first two at the residence of the APSAD’s President Ms. Raya Daouk and the last at the residence of General Michel Aoun June 21, 2014.

Were present at these three meetings:

Mr Paul Abi Rached, President of Lebanon Eco Movement (LEM), a gathering of 60 environmental NGOs, which includes APSAD.

Mr Pierre Doumet, President of the Association for the Protection of Jabal Moussa (APJM)

Ms. Joelle Barakat, a member of the Association for the Protection of Jabal Moussa

Experts: Dr. Myrna Habre (biologist), Dr. Raymond Gèze (geologist), Dr Wilson Rizk (physicist), Dr. Janine Somma (geographer)

Mr. Saadeh Saadeh, Lebanon Eco Movement

Mrs Nelly Abdallah and Gladys Nader, SOS Environment of APSAD Committee.

The experts explained the reasons why the Janneh dam presents a danger to water resources to the valley of Nahr Brahim and his remains, for biodiversity and for man.
NGOs demand to stop work until there is a serious study on the matter.

In this regard General Aoun took note of the problem. He will study the issue before making a decision.

title: Kfardebiane natural bridge
summary: Happy ending for the Kfardebiane Natural Bridge Affair At last, dear friends, we have good news to share with you: the Kfardebiane Natural Bridge is saved from illegal construction, after 19 years of action! When we discovered the offense…
content:
Happy ending for the Kfardebiane Natural Bridge Affair

At last, dear friends, we have good news to share with you: the Kfardebiane Natural Bridge is saved from illegal construction, after 19 years of action!
When we discovered the offense on this protected site during a hike in 1994,
we started working with Gaby Bustros and SOS Environnement on alert campaigns, authorities interventions, media coverage and even justice.
Finally, the promoter has lost his appeal (14.1.2013) to Majlis al Choura
(Council of State) against the Ministry of Environnement who had stopped
his project.

The last action organized on the Bridge: a press conference and a hike on 8.8.2009 with 30 other associations, boosted once again the public’s interest. Finally and most importantly, APSAD’s decision to act as a third party in the lawsuit, besides the Ministry of Environment, was decisive in the issue.
We wish to thank deeply all our friends for their support, with whom we worked hard: Dr Berge Hadjian, D.G. of the Ministry of Environment for his strong position, the NGOs for their cooperation, Maitre Abdallah Zakhia for his precious legal advice, and of course the medias with their greatly dedicated journalists.

This case is unique in Lebanon: it is the first time that a promoter is stopped in the destruction of a heritage site by activists, and his legal action rejected by justice.

Such a success teaches us a lesson: to reach your goal, you need patience, faith and participation of all concerned: authorities, civil society and medias.

Gladys Nader and Nelly Abdallah
SOS Environnement Commitee- APSAD
6 march 2013

title: Protection of old buildings
summary: Good news to APSAD members July 2010.The Minister of Culture Mr. Selim Wardy, gave a press conference dedicated to the protection of old buildings, at UNESCO PALACE on Wednesday July 1st, 2010.Several decisions were announced to this…
content:
Good news to APSAD members July 2010.

The Minister of Culture Mr. Selim Wardy, gave a press conference dedicated to the protection of old buildings, at UNESCO PALACE on Wednesday July 1st, 2010.

Several decisions were announced to this effect:

►Mr. Wardy has firmly decided to adopt a law for the preservation of old buildings. This law
project, initiated by APSAD and worked upon for many years, is presently blocked at the Parliament.

►Mr. Wardy acted with the government and obtained their consentment that this project becomes a priority to be voted soonest.

►Awaiting the vote of this law, he decided that all destructions will be forbidden without
his personal authorisation , and in accordance with the Ministry of Interior.

►He declared that a hotline bearing the number of 01.612299 will be at the disposal of
the citizens who should contact the Ministry of Culture for any violation of the law.

►He announced the launching of a media campaign, starting with a video clip - produced by
the company Grey-to be broadcasted by all TVs.

►He invited all concerned partners to support the execution of his project by all means, even by sit-ins if necessary.

title: Kfardebaine stone bridge
summary: Campaign for the protection of the Kfardebian Stone Bridge More than 250 persons from all over Lebanon, representing 26 NGOs, participated to the gathering organised on Saturday 8th August 2009 by the "SOS Environment" Committee of APSAD…
content:
Campaign for the protection of the Kfardebian Stone Bridge

More than 250 persons from all over Lebanon, representing 26 NGOs, participated to the gathering organised on Saturday 8th August 2009 by the "SOS Environment" Committee of APSAD.

The participants walked in the area around the Natural Bridge- one of the biggest in the world- while the organisers explained its geological and natural interest. The press conference was given in the presence of several officials by Miss. Gladys Nader, who explained the importance of a permanent preservation of this protected site threatened by a construction project. It was followed by a mini-concert of ecological songs.

The event received a good media coverage. Among the organisers, Maxime Chaya gave his full support, along with the NGOs Baldati, Speleo Club du Liban, Lebanon Mountain Trail, T.E.R.R.E Liban, Vamos Todos etc.

title: Campaign to save 7 houses in Tabet Street
summary: 20 Mars 2009 : On 20 March 2009 Apsad launched a campaign to save seven historical houses in Beirut, namely in Tabet Street, Achrafieh. The campaign proved quite successful, with hundreds supporting the petition to safeguard our urban…
content:
20 Mars 2009 : On 20 March 2009
Apsad launched a campaign to save seven historical
houses in Beirut, namely in Tabet Street, Achrafieh.

The campaign proved quite successful, with hundreds supporting the petition to safeguard our urban heritage, fighting against the destruction of these historical buildings. It is imperative that our society as a whole be made aware of our unique heritage, working towards the preservation

and restoration of old houses against the overwhelming tide
of unsightly developments and high-rise apartments.

APSAD strives to maintain the unique urban fibre of our capital,
enhancing the beauty of its traditional dwellings, attracting ecological
tourism while encouraging sensible urban development that respects our heritage and identity.

APSAD presented a petition signed by hundreds supporters to save the seven old historical houses in Achrafieh Tabet street.

content:
ADG Expo 2008 - August 2008

Under the Patronage of H.E. the President of the Republic General Michel Sleiman , the ADG’s 15th Art Exhibition took place between the 20th and the 24th of August 2008. APSAD participated in this event by presenting the following publications:

« l’Habitation au Liban » by Jacques Liger-Belair,
a book about Lebanese Architecture ;

« Connaissance du Liban » by Samia Kfouri Nassar about Lebanon’s historical places ;

« Sel du Liban » by Hafez Jureige, about the preparation
of Lebanese Salt;

“Centre Ville” de May Abboud Abi
Akl regarding the excavations of the Down Town
District and finally

“Diversity of moths in Lebanon”
by Abdul Mun’im Talhouk, about the insects’ Role in
the Environement.
